featuredTips.title: Light The Eyes First
featuredTips.summary: If your subject's eyes catch a small specular highlight, the whole frame reads alive. Place a soft key 30° off-axis at eye level — adjust until you see a 2 o'clock catchlight.

featuredTips.title: Audio Is 70% Of Video
featuredTips.summary: A blurry shot with crisp audio plays. A sharp shot with bad audio dies in 3 seconds. Lav your subject, set levels at -12dB peaks, and always run a backup recorder.

featuredTips.title: Shoot The Cutaway
featuredTips.summary: Every interview needs B-roll. Hands, environment, gear, gestures — anything. It saves your edit when you need to cut a stutter or cover a jump cut.

featuredTips.title: Frame For The Crop
featuredTips.summary: Shooting in 16:9 but delivering 9:16? Compose with the vertical safe area in mind from day one. Place subjects on the center third — never the edges.
